label: Arpeggiator
description: A MIDI device: plays the notes held in a shape (up, down, played, chord, random...) or a drawn pattern whose rows are the held notes, so it follows any chord, with chance, ratchets, conditions, scale steps, swing and a range of shifted passes; twelve pattern slots. Vintergatan's arp is the same.

label: Note Repeater
description: A MIDI device: repeats each note, as a delay repeats sound, up to sixteen times, each repeat a step later, moved in pitch from the one before and louder or softer. With no time between them the repeats stack into chords.

label: Key Chords
description: A MIDI device: keeps each note to a key and scale, moving one outside it to the nearest scale note or silencing it, and can play each as a chord of the scale, of one to five notes stacked in its thirds, inverted or opened, with an octave above or below and a colour on top.

label: Drum Grid
description: A MIDI device: plays eight channels of sixteen steps as the song plays, each a key of the instrument such as a drum rack's pad, with eight patterns to choose between. Each channel has its own length, speed, direction and slide, and each step a velocity, repeats, triplets or a flam, and a probability. The track's own notes pass through.

label: Twin Arpeggiator
description: A MIDI device: two arpeggiators side by side, each over the held notes in its own range of keys, up, down, up and down or at random over one to four octaves, or as a pattern of up to four notes a step, with a velocity lane, a gate, and a hold. Notes outside both ranges pass through.

label: Anchor Arpeggiator
description: A MIDI device: an arpeggio of two parts, an anchor that plays one to three of the chord's notes in a sparse, repeating rhythm, and a movement that runs through the others between them in one of forty shapes, as thick as its density says, with rhythm and octave modifiers chosen by a seed.

label: Note Filter
description: A MIDI device: lets through the notes within a range of keys and of velocities, or outside it, and moves, fixes or scales their pitch, octave, velocity on a curve, and length, limits how many sound at once, and holds them.

label: Note Chance
description: A MIDI device: lets notes through by a sequence of yes and no, or by chance, and by chance sets or moves their pitch, velocity and length within ranges, each with a chance of its own or one for all.

label: Rhythm Map
description: A MIDI device: plays drum patterns from a map of rhythms as the song plays. Where on the map it stands sets how plain or syncopated its kick and snare are, a density for each of four drums thins or fills them, and each drum has a mirror that plays between its hits. The track's own notes pass through.

label: Euclid Lines
description: A MIDI device: four lines that each play a Euclidean rhythm at a rate of their own, with pitches, velocities and lengths varied by chance about a base key, kept to a scale, frozen in a zone, and joined as chords or as one line. It plays with the song, or while a key is held, about that key.

label: Chord Steps
description: A MIDI device: a polyphonic step sequencer in a scale, whose notes can be boxes that play chords, repeats, arpeggios or strums, with eight patterns of four variations each that switch by themselves, a velocity lane, and transposition from the keys.

label: Pattern Variations
description: A MIDI device: plays a polyphonic pattern of steps, and makes variations of it at a click: notes moved by octaves and fifths or further, swapped, thinned or filled, lengthened, and accented. Eight patterns, transposed from the keys.

label: Chord Pads
description: A MIDI device: sixteen chords on pads, from sets in many styles or written by hand, each lit by how well it would follow the last, played from the keys or by a progression of up to sixteen bars, with velocity, humanizing, a bass taken away or a root added, and eight patterns.

label: Bassline Maker
description: A MIDI device: makes a bass line of an on-beat phrase and an off-beat one, chosen from busy to sparse and varied through the pattern, its intervals stretched and made minor, transposed from the keys or played as written, with eight patterns.

label: Transpose
description: A MIDI device: moves the track's notes by steps of a scale, by semitones, and by octaves before the instrument plays them, in the project's scale or one of its own.

label: SID
summary: three-voice chip synth in the style of the 1980s home-computer sound chip: pulses, arps, sync and ring-modulated tones
description: A three-voice chip synth with clocked oscillators and ADSR, pulse width, sync, ring modulation, and a shared filter. Poly or unison; two chip models and PAL/NTSC clocks. An approximate SID sound engine.

label: Vireo
summary: wavetable and virtual analogue synth: hard leads, supersaw-style stacks, pads and basses
description: A wavetable and virtual analogue synth of the early 2000s German kind: two Classic oscillators with sub, third oscillator, noise and ring, two multimode filters with an analogue ladder, four envelopes, three LFOs, a six-slot matrix and unison, wave and HyperSaw oscillator modes and its effects. Its state is the original's 512-byte Single, and its own SysEx patches and banks load. Another track's audio is its external input.

label: Basic Synth
description: A plain oscillator voice: sine, saw, square, or triangle.

label: Vintergatan
description: The flagship synth: three oscillators, each a wavetable that morphs and bends, an analog oscillator that drifts, syncs and is bent by the first, a sample or grains of one; a sub, noise, and another track's audio; two filters in series, in parallel, split, or each source to its own; six envelopes, ten LFOs, sixteen macros, a matrix of 64 routes, five ways of unison (each voice at twice the rate, or in Eco, as the preferences choose for playing, at the rate with its modulation worked out every 16 samples), a chain of any of Solmara's effects after its voices, and two FX busses, bus1 and bus2, each a chain its oscillators, sub, noise, input and filters send to.

label: Kick
description: A kick drum of five layers, each a body (a sine blended with a waveform and a wavetable), a click, noise, or a sample or factory click, shaped over the hit by curves of pitch, level, and place in the table, with points that follow the key and lock the phase; velocity, random, and LFO, drive, tone, and a limiter. Its layers go to bus A, bus B, or straight on, and its chains busA, busB, and master hold effects for each, the master's for what they come to.

label: Mini Moonbeam
summary: three-oscillator monosynth in the style of the early-1970s American portables: fat bass and singing leads
description: A modelled three-oscillator monosynth of the early 1970s, built from its circuit and fitted to a reference by measurement: three free-running oscillators with ranges in feet (LO, 32' to 2') and the circuit's waveforms (triangle, shark-tooth or reverse saw, saw, three pulses), noise white or pink, and a five-input mixer that overdrives the filter, into a transistor ladder and two contours. One voice with low-note priority, a single trigger, and glide. The filter and the contours are plain stand-ins until they are fitted.

label: Shy One
summary: one-oscillator monosynth in the style of the early-1980s Japanese portables: punchy bass and acid lines
description: A modelled one-oscillator monosynth of the early 1980s, built from its circuit and fitted to a reference by measurement: one oscillator with its saw, a pulse with its width by hand, by the LFO or by the envelope, a sub-oscillator one or two octaves down or a narrow pulse, and noise, each by its slider, into a four-pole transconductance low-pass that sings at full resonance and an amplifier opened by the envelope or the gate. One envelope, started by the gate and each key, by the gate alone, or by the LFO; an LFO of four waveforms to the pitch, the pulse width and the filter; portamento always or between keys held together; the bender and its push to the LFO. The last key struck sounds.

label: Reed Electric Piano
summary: reed electric piano in the style of the 1960s American classroom pianos: bell-like and nasal, barking when played hard, with tremolo
description: A modelled reed electric piano of the late 1960s and the 1970s, built from its physics: a felt hammer strikes a steel reed tuned by the solder at its tip, which rings in its three bending modes, far from harmonic, the harder the strike the brighter. Each reed swings through the slot of a charged comb, a capacitor whose bell-shaped law turns a hard-struck key's swing into its bark. A preamp that clips softly and unevenly, the instrument's tremolo through a lamp and a photoresistor, a tone, and its small speakers or the line out. Dampers on all but the top keys, the sustain pedal (CC 64), and the keys' thump.

label: String Ensemble
summary: string ensemble in the style of the 1970s string machines: lush string pads and swelling brass, thickened by the ensemble chorus
description: A modelled string ensemble keyboard of the 1970s, fitted to a reference by measurement: a divide-down organ, every key always running from one master clock, keyed through its own crescendo and sustain; violin, viola, trumpet and horn on every key and contrabass and cello on the lower keys, each register a fixed filter; and the ensemble, three bucket-brigade lines swept by a slow and a fast oscillator, in mono or stereo. A choir register and an LFO for vibrato and tremolo, which its reference adds.

label: Electric Clavichord
summary: electric clavichord in the style of the 1970s German funk keyboards: nasal and percussive, with its pickup and tone switches and mute
description: A modelled electric clavichord of the 1960s and 1970s, built from its physics and held to a reference by measurement: a rubber tangent strikes each steel string and holds it against an anvil while the key is down, the harder the brighter, and the string rings between the tangent and the bridge, a little stiff, its upper partials sharp. Let go, the string is its whole length in the yarn, and sounds its release's thunk a little lower as the yarn takes it down. Two electromagnetic pickups under the strings and their two rocker switches, one pickup or the other or both in and out of phase; the four tone switches, filters that add; the mute slider. 24 strings sound at once.

label: Titan 303
summary: Titan 303 in the style of the early-1980s Japanese bass machines: squelching lines with accent and slide
description: A modelled acid bass line synthesizer of the early 1980s, built from its circuit and fitted to a reference by measurement: one oscillator, its saw or the square a waveshaper makes from it, into a four-pole diode-ladder low-pass and an amplifier. A decay-only envelope on the filter by its amount and decay, and a fixed one on the amplifier. Played by notes: a velocity of 100 or more accents a note, louder and brighter, accents in a row building through the accent's sweep; a note struck while another is held slides to its pitch. A drive after it: off, or the overdrive or the distortion pedal's circuit.

label: Tonewheel Organ
summary: tonewheel organ in the style of the mid-century American console organs: drawbars, percussion and click for gospel, jazz and rock
description: A modelled tonewheel organ of the late 1950s, built from its mechanism: 91 tonewheels on one motor through twelve gear ratios, so its tuning is near equal temperament and not on it; nine drawbars on each of two manuals and two on the pedals, with the foldback at the ends; contacts that close apart and bounce, which is the key click; the wiring's leakage; the percussion of the second or third harmonic, soft or normal, fast or slow, struck only when no key is held; the scanner vibrato and chorus V1 to C3; the preamp's drive and the expression pedal. Every key sounds at once.

label: Tine Electric Piano
summary: tine electric piano in the style of the 1970s American suitcase pianos: bell-like ballads to barking funk, with stereo tremolo
description: A modelled tine electric piano of the 1970s, built from how it makes its sound and held to a reference by measurement: a felt hammer strikes a steel tine on its tone bar, which rings as a few modes in front of an electromagnetic pickup whose flux bends what it hears, a bell when played softly and a bark when played hard; a damper on each key, the sustain pedal, and the key's and the damper's knock. The stage model's passive output, or the suitcase model's preamp, bass and treble, stereo tremolo, amplifier and speakers. 32 tines sound at once.

label: Six-Op FM
summary: six-operator FM synth in the style of the 1980s Japanese digital keyboards: bells, electric pianos, basses and brass
description: A modelled six-operator FM synthesizer of 1983, its digital engine's behaviour held to a reference by measurement: six sine operators in one of 32 algorithms, each at a ratio of the key's pitch or a fixed frequency, with its output level and an envelope of four rates and four levels; one operator feeds itself back. Sixteen voices.

label: Two-Filter Mono
summary: semi-modular two-filter monosynth in the style of the late-1970s Japanese patch synths: screaming peaks, ring-modulated leads and bass
description: A modelled semi-modular monosynth of the late 1970s, built from its circuit and fitted to a reference by measurement: two oscillators, the first with its triangle, saw, pulse of a width by hand and white noise, the second with its saw, square, narrow pulse and the ring modulator of the two, by a pitch knob of its own, each by its level into a high-pass and a low-pass in series, each with its cutoff and its peak, and an amplifier. Two envelopes, EG 1 (delay, attack, release) to the pitch and EG 2 (hold, attack, decay, sustain, release) to the filters and the amplifier; an MG from a falling saw through a triangle to a rising one, to the pitch and the filters; portamento. Its normalled routing; the filters, the envelopes and the MG are plain stand-ins until they are fitted.

label: Promise Bloom
summary: five-voice polysynth in the style of the late-1970s American programmable synths: warm pads, brass, and poly leads
description: A modelled five-voice polysynth of the late 1970s, built from its circuit and fitted to a reference by measurement: each voice two oscillators, A with its saw and pulse and sync to B, B with its saw, triangle and pulse, a low-frequency mode and the keyboard on or off, and noise, into a four-pole low-pass that sings at full resonance and an amplifier, each on an envelope of its own. Poly-Mod takes the filter's envelope and oscillator B to A's pitch and pulse width and to the filter; the mod wheel takes the LFO and the noise to either oscillator and the filter. Glide, unison, and a release switch.

label: Juniper Eight
summary: eight-voice polysynth in the style of the early-1980s Japanese flagships: brass, pads, sync leads and split or layered patches
description: A modelled eight-voice polysynth of the early 1980s, built from its circuit and held to a reference by measurement: each voice two oscillators, the first with its triangle, saw, pulse and square and cross-modulation from the second, the second with its sine, saw, pulse and noise, sync either way, a source mix into a high-pass and a four-pole low-pass switchable to two poles that sings at full resonance, and an amplifier, on two envelopes that follow the keys if asked. An LFO with its delay to the oscillators, the pulse width, the filter and the amplifier. An upper and a lower patch, played whole, dual or split; solo, unison and two poly modes; hold, portamento and an arpeggiator.

label: Cosmos 80
summary: two-layer polysynth in the style of the late-1970s Japanese flagship: expressive brass, soundtrack pads and per-key pressure
description: A modelled eight-voice polysynth of the late 1970s whose every voice is two whole synthesizers layered, held to a reference by measurement: each channel a VCO with its saw, its square and its pulse-width LFO, noise and a sine beside the filters, a high-pass and a low-pass in series each with its resonance, a filter envelope from its initial level to its attack level, and an ADSR. The strike brightens, raises and bends each note; each key's own pressure brightens and raises it and drives the sub-oscillator's speed, vibrato and filter swing on it. Keyboard control of brilliance and level, a sub-oscillator, a ring modulator with its own envelope, detune, portamento or glissando, a ribbon, and a chorus or tremolo.

label: Cosine Zone
summary: phase-distortion synth in the style of the mid-1980s Japanese home keyboards: glassy pads, resonant sweeps, bright basses and bells
description: A modelled phase-distortion synth of the mid-1980s Japanese home keyboards, held to a reference by measurement: two lines, each a cosine read through a bent phase (saw, square, pulse, double sine, saw-pulse and three resonance waves, one or two in alternate cycles), with 8-step envelopes on its pitch, its bend (DCW) and its level (DCA), key follow, ring and noise modulation, line detune, vibrato, portamento and the DAC's colour. Eight voices, four with both lines.

label: Oberon Eight
summary: eight-voice polysynth in the style of the early-1980s American polys: big brass stabs, fat pads, sync leads and split or doubled patches
description: A modelled eight-voice polysynth of the early 1980s, built from its circuit and held to a reference by measurement: each voice two chip oscillators, each a saw and a pulse that may sound together, sync and cross-modulation, a mixer with noise into a four-pole low-pass switchable to a two-pole state-variable, and an amplifier, each on its own envelope. An LFO by two depths to the frequencies, the filter, the pulse widths and the amplifier, and the lever's vibrato. An upper and a lower patch, played whole, double or split; unison, hold and portamento.

label: Arcturus 2600
summary: semi-modular monosynth in the style of the early-1970s American studio synths: sample-and-hold bleeps, resonant basses, ring-modulated bells, sync leads and effects patched on the panel
description: A modelled semi-modular monosynth of the early 1970s, built from its circuit and held to a reference by measurement, its normalled routing the default patch: three oscillators (saws, a square, a triangle, a sine and pulses, sync and frequency modulation between them), noise with its colour, a ring modulator, a four-pole low-pass to singing, an ADSR and an AR, an amplifier with linear and exponential inputs, a mixer with pan and spring reverb, a sample-and-hold on its clock, an envelope follower and a lag. The common patch cords are panel choices. One voice, or two on the keyboard's lower and upper keys; portamento and delayed vibrato.

label: Jet-8000
summary: ten-voice virtual-analogue synth in the style of the late-1990s Japanese dance synths: Super Saw, Unison and SysEx patch import
description: A ten-voice, two-part digital synthesizer: Super Saw and six other oscillator modes, sync, cross and ring modulation, a 12/24 dB multimode filter, three envelopes, two LFOs, Unison, velocity destinations, multi-effects and delay, the ribbon and the arpeggiator. Imports original patches and performances. Another track's audio is its external input, which OSC2 External and the Voice Modulator play.

label: Norrsken
summary: virtual-analogue polysynth in the style of the late-1990s Scandinavian keyboards: leads, sync sweeps, and morphing pads
description: A modelled twenty-voice virtual-analogue synthesizer from Stockholm, of the turn of the century: its digital engine held to a reference by measurement and blind listening: two oscillators with sync, linear FM and ring modulation, a filter of five types with distortion, three envelopes, two LFOs (the second an arpeggiator or an echo), velocity and wheel morphs on every knob, unison, and the wheel, the stick, aftertouch and a pedal as the hardware takes them. Imports the hardware's documented SysEx programs.

label: June Bloom
summary: six-voice polysynth with chorus in the style of the early-1980s Japanese polys: lush pads, stabs, and bass
description: A modelled six-voice polysynth of the mid-1980s, built from its circuit and fitted to a reference by measurement: each voice a digitally clocked oscillator, its saw, a pulse from it with its width by hand or by the LFO, a square sub-oscillator an octave down, and noise, into a four-pole transconductance low-pass that sings at full resonance and an amplifier opened by the voice's envelope or its gate; then a stepped high-pass and the bucket-brigade chorus. One LFO with a delay, a bender to the pitch, the filter and the LFO, and two ways of giving out the voices.

label: PH-8
summary: analogue drum machine in the style of the early-1980s Japanese rhythm composers: sixteen sounds for electro, hip-hop and house
description: The analogue drum machine of the early 1980s as one instrument: its sixteen sounds on their General MIDI keys, the bridged-T kick, the snare, three toms and three congas, the rim shot and the claves, the hand clap and the maracas, the cowbell, the cymbal and the two hats, the closed one cutting the open; each sound's own knobs, the machine's accent and its volume. It expands into a drum rack of its voices, for an effect on one sound.

label: PH-8 Part
summary: the PH-8 one channel at a time: kick, snare, toms, congas, rim, claves, clap, maracas, cowbell, cymbal and hats
description: One channel of the PH-8 alone, for a pad of a drum rack: the tabs on its face choose which, the bass drum, snare, toms and congas, rim shot and claves, clap and maracas, cowbell, cymbal and hats, each keeping its own knobs; any key strikes it.

label: Slice Player
description: A loop cut into parts at its hits, each part on a key with its own pitch, level, pan, decay and reverse, named by what it sounds like; it writes a drum pattern that plays the loop, to remix it in the drum editor. A filter with an LFO, poly or choke voices, and a held tail for slower tempos.

label: Sampler
description: Plays a sample library where it lies on the disk, its long samples streamed from there: SFZ and DecentSampler, with Kontakt to come. Its knobs are the library's MIDI controllers and its volume.

label: Granular Sampler
description: A sample played as windowed grains: position and scan, size and density, spray, pitch, freeze, stereo scatter, an amplitude envelope and LFO modulation; 16 voices and 128 grains.

label: PH-6
summary: small analogue drum machine in the style of the early-1980s Japanese compact boxes: seven sounds, light and ticking
description: The small analogue drum machine of the early 1980s as one instrument: its seven sounds on their General MIDI keys, the kick, the snare, the low and high toms, the cymbal and the open and closed hats, the closed one cutting the open; each sound's own knobs, the machine's accent and its volume. It expands into a drum rack of its voices, for an effect on one sound.

label: PH-6 Part
summary: the PH-6 one channel at a time: kick, snare, toms, cymbal and hats
description: One channel of the PH-6 alone, for a pad of a drum rack: the tabs on its face choose which, the bass drum, snare, low and high toms, cymbal and hats, each keeping its own knobs; any key strikes it.

label: PH-9
summary: analogue and sampled drum machine in the style of the mid-1980s Japanese rhythm composers: eleven sounds for house and techno
description: The drum machine of the mid-1980s as one instrument: its eleven sounds on their General MIDI keys, the kick with its attack, the snare, three toms, the rim shot and the hand clap, and the closed and open hats, the crash and the ride, the closed hat cutting the open; each sound's own knobs, the machine's total accent and its volume. It expands into a drum rack of its voices, for an effect on one sound.

label: PH-9 Part
summary: the PH-9 one channel at a time: kick, snare, toms, rim, clap, hats, crash and ride
description: One channel of the PH-9 alone, for a pad of a drum rack: the tabs on its face choose which, the bass drum, snare, three toms, rim shot, clap, hats, crash and ride, each keeping its own knobs; any key strikes it.

label: Simple Sampler
description: Plays one sample from a root note, with trim, forward looping and an ADSR amplitude envelope.

label: Utility
description: Gain, pan, and a DC offset.

label: Polarnatt Clipper
summary: mastering clipper: peaks off before the limiter, in six curves
description: A clipper for the master and for buses, the mastering family's: it drives the audio into a ceiling it never passes, to take the fastest peaks off before a limiter, more cleanly than a limiter can. Its algorithm is how it bends into the ceiling, from hard through soft, sine, a diode pair's and tape's to a valve's lopsided curve, its softness how far under the ceiling it starts, and it runs at once, four, or sixteen times the rate so what it makes does not fold back.

label: Bitcrusher
description: Takes fewer samples a second and keeps each to fewer bits: grit and alias of early samplers.

label: Ring Modulator
description: Multiplies the audio by a carrier, a sine, triangle, or square, for metallic and bell tones.

label: Frequency Shifter
description: Moves every partial of the audio by the same number of hertz, up or down: unlike a pitch shift, the harmonics stop being harmonic, from a slow phasing swirl at a few hertz to bell and robot tones; the right channel can go the other way.

label: Waveshaper
description: Bends the audio through a curve, tanh, a folder, a sine, an asymmetric one, or hard, met off its middle by the bias, at twice the rate.

label: Mono Bass
description: Makes everything under a frequency mono and leaves what is above it as it was.

label: Morgonrodnad EQ
summary: parametric EQ: eight bands, in stereo, mid and side, or linear phase
description: The parametric EQ, the mastering family's: eight bands of low cut, shelf, bell, notch, and high cut filters, each on both sides, their middle, or their side. Shelves and bells can cut or boost dynamically from their band level or another track by sidechain. In linear phase it draws the same curve and leaves the phase alone, some 85 ms late.

label: Gate
description: Turns down audio below a threshold, with smooth attack and release, hold, and hysteresis. Its filtered detector can listen to another track before or after that track's fader.

label: Vocoder
description: Makes a carrier speak through 4 to 40 bands of an input's envelopes. Noise, external audio, the input itself, or a pitch-following oscillator; with formants, freeze, and a band patchbay.

label: Compressor
description: Evens out level: turns down what rises above a threshold, by a ratio. It can listen to another track by sidechain, through a filter, so a kick ducks a bass.

label: Molnlucka
summary: room maker: its track's bands cut where another track plays
description: Makes room in its track for another, band by band: it listens to the other track by sidechain and turns its own track down in each of 32 bands by as much as the other is loud there, so a vocal comes through the guitars without the guitars ducked as a whole. Amount, attack and release, the range it cuts in, only where the two clash, and each side cut by where the other sits. No latency.

label: Leveltron Solid State
summary: solid-state opto compressor in the style of the late-1960s American levelers: a faster, firmer grip for guitars, drums and vocals
description: A modelled solid-state optical compressor-limiter: a transistor amplifier whose input a photoresistor turns down as a light driven by the audio brightens. Two knobs, how much it turns down and how loud it comes out, a switch from compressing to limiting, and an HF emphasis that has it level the highs more; threshold, ratio, attack, and release come of the light and the cell. Modelled on the transistor successor of the valve leveller, from the late 1960s: the same kind of cell, a faster grip and a brighter, firmer sound, for guitars, drums, bass and vocals.

label: Leveltron Opto
summary: valve opto leveler in the style of the 1960s American broadcast levelers: smooth, slow levelling for vocals and bass
description: A modelled optical levelling amplifier: a valve amplifier whose input a photoresistor turns down as a light driven by the audio brightens. Two knobs, how much it turns down and how loud it comes out, a switch from compressing to limiting, and an emphasis that has it level the highs more; threshold, ratio, attack, and release are not set but come of the light and the cell. Modelled on the two-knob valve leveller of the 1960s that studios put on vocals and bass: slow, smooth, and forgiving. It takes far more processing than the compressor.

label: Danish Blue Compressor
summary: valve opto compressor in the style of the 1980s Danish studio units: transparent control for mixes and mastering
description: A modelled optical compressor with a valve make-up amplifier: a photoresistor lit by the sidechain turns the audio down ahead of the amplifier. Threshold, ratio, attack, release, and gain, with fixed, manual, or combined timing, and a switch that takes the valves out for a clean amplifier at a fraction of the processing. Modelled on the blue-faced Danish valve opto compressor of the 1980s, a usual choice on vocals, bass, and a mix bus for gain reduction that is hard to hear.

label: Push-Pull EQ
summary: passive valve EQ in the style of the 1950s American program equalisers: broad lows and silky highs
description: A modelled passive program equaliser with a valve make-up amplifier: a low shelf that boosts and cuts at once, a peak in the highs with a bandwidth knob, and a high cut, all in one network of pots, capacitors, and a coil, whose sections lean on each other. A switch takes the valves and the transformers out for a clean amplifier at a fraction of the processing. Modelled on the passive valve program equaliser of the 1950s, known for boosting and cutting the lows at once, a lift with a dip above it, for kicks and basses, and for a broad, smooth high boost.

label: Push-Pull Midrange EQ
summary: passive valve mid-range EQ in the style of the late-1950s American units: a low peak, a dip and a high peak for body, boxiness and presence
description: A modelled passive mid-range equaliser with a valve make-up amplifier: a low peak from 200 Hz to 1 kHz, a dip from 200 Hz to 7 kHz, and a high peak from 1.5 to 5 kHz, each a coil and a capacitor on a switch, in one network whose sections lean on each other. A switch takes the valves and the transformers out for a clean amplifier at a fraction of the processing. Modelled on the passive valve mid-range equaliser of the late 1950s, the program equaliser's companion, for the body of a voice or a guitar, a dip for the boxiness of a drum, and presence.

label: Passive Program Filter
summary: passive high- and low-cut filter in the style of the 1950s American program filters: stepped LC sections for rumble, hiss and telephone effects
description: A modelled passive high- and low-cut filter with no amplifier: a low cut from 50 Hz to 2 kHz and a high cut from 1.5 to 15 kHz, each a coil and capacitor section on a stepped switch, the two loading each other, and a key to throw it in and out. Modelled on the American program filters of the 1950s and 1960s, for rumble and hiss, a thinned or telephone-like voice, or a dark, distant effect.

label: Wreck Stack
summary: high-gain valve head in the style of the 1990s American metal amps: modern rhythm and lead
description: A modelled high-gain guitar amplifier, without a cabinet: stacked valve stages that hand their clipping on to each other, a tone stack, and a push-pull power stage on a speaker's load. Gain, bass, mid, treble, presence, and master, a clean channel and a lead one, a mode switch that takes the feedback off the power stage, a supply held stiff or rectified by silicon or by valves, which sag under a loud note, at the full voltage or a lowered one, and a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuit is solved. It wants a cabinet after it, the speaker cabinet device: alone it is harsh. Modelled on the two-channel American high-gain valve head of the 1990s with a choice of rectifiers, the sound of that decade's heavy guitars.

label: Convolution Reverb
description: A recorded space from a user-loaded impulse response, with sample-accurate trim, pre-delay, damping, mix and level. A second stereo response in the right slot makes four true-stereo paths. Responses are kept in the project; up to 30 seconds are used. Without a primary response it passes audio unchanged.

label: Boxed Twelves
summary: 4x12 speaker cabinet: the miked box after any amp
description: A guitar speaker cabinet with its microphone, to follow a guitar amplifier: a closed box of four twelve-inch speakers, as a row of filters fitted to measured cabinets, in two voicings, forward and thick, with the microphone's place across the cone, the box's resonance, and its size. Low and high cuts, phase, mix, and level. It holds the audio back by nothing. For a cabinet of your own, as an impulse response, use Cabinet IR.

label: Cabinet IR
summary: guitar cabinet from an impulse response of your own
description: Any guitar speaker cabinet, as an impulse response loaded from a WAV file, which is kept with the project and applied by convolution: how much of it is used, low and high cuts, phase, mix, and level. Without a response it passes the audio unchanged. It holds the audio back by nothing.

label: Green Overdrive Pedal
summary: mid-hump overdrive pedal in the style of the late-1970s Japanese green overdrives: tightens a high-gain amp
description: A modelled overdrive pedal that lifts the middle of a guitar's band: an operational amplifier with two diodes back to back in its feedback, which clips softly and only what lies above the lows, so the low end passes clean and stays tight, then a tone control and a level. Drive, tone, and level, with a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuits are solved. With the drive low and the level high it is the boost put in front of a high-gain amplifier to tighten rhythm playing. Modelled on the small green overdrive pedal of the late 1970s, named for making a valve amplifier scream, the usual pedal before a high-gain head.

label: Metal District Pedal
summary: high-gain distortion pedal in the style of the early-1990s Japanese metal pedals: scooped, saturated metal
description: A modelled high-gain distortion pedal with an equaliser of its own: a resonant stage lifts the upper middle round 1 kHz before a gain stage and two diodes to ground clip it hard, a second resonant stage lifts the lows round 100 Hz and the top round 5 kHz after, and then an active equaliser with a high, a low, and a middle of 15 dB either way whose frequency is swept from some 180 Hz to 6 kHz. Dist, level, high, low, middle, and middle frequency, a hiss knob for the circuit's own noise, and a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuits are solved. It is made to be played into a clean amplifier, and with its middle cut it is the scooped sound of 1990s metal. Modelled on the orange and black distortion pedal of the early 1990s, named for a zone of metal, with its two concentric equaliser knobs.

label: British Crunch Head
summary: master-volume valve head in the style of the early-1980s British rock amps: crunch and lead
description: A modelled British master-volume guitar head of one channel, without a cabinet: an input valve, a cold-biased second stage that clips one side of the wave first, a third stage into a cathode follower, a passive tone stack whose knobs lean on each other, a master before the phase inverter, and four European output pentodes in push-pull on a speaker's load, with the presence in the power stage's feedback loop. Preamp, bass, middle, treble, presence, and master, a high input and a low one that passes the input valve by, and a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuit is solved. It wants a cabinet after it, the speaker cabinet device. Modelled on the British 100-watt master-volume lead head of the early 1980s, the crunch and lead sound of that decade's hard rock.

label: 1960s Blues Combo
summary: valve combo in the style of the mid-1960s British 2x12 combos: warm breakup for blues-rock, with tremolo
description: A modelled British guitar combo of the mid-1960s, without its speakers: the jumpered head's circuit of two channels and four input jacks, with its own numbers, two beam tetrodes in push-pull, no capacitor across the first channel's volume, and a tremolo on the second channel. Two volumes, bass, middle, treble, presence, the tremolo's intensity and speed, which jack the guitar is in and whether a jumper joins the channels, and a quality switch. It wants a cabinet after it, the speaker cabinet device. Modelled on the British 2x12 combo of the mid-1960s that blues-rock broke up through.

label: British Jumper Head
summary: jumpered valve head in the style of the late-1960s British 100-watt amps: loud, open classic rock
description: A modelled British guitar head of two channels and no master volume, without a cabinet: four input jacks, a high and a low for a normal channel and a bright one, into the two halves of the input valve; a volume for each, the bright one with a large capacitor that lifts the top the more the lower it is turned; the two mixed into a second stage coupled to a cathode follower, a passive tone stack whose knobs lean on each other, and four European output pentodes in push-pull on a speaker's load, with the presence in the power stage's feedback loop. With no master the volumes drive the power stage as well, and turned up it is the power stage that distorts. Bright and normal volumes, bass, middle, treble, presence, which jack the guitar is in and whether a jumper joins the channels, and a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuit is solved. It wants a cabinet after it, the speaker cabinet device. Modelled on the British 100-watt lead head of the late 1960s with its clear front panel, the loud, open crunch of that era's rock, cleaner than a master-volume head at the same settings.

label: British Chime Combo
summary: chiming 30-watt combo in the style of the 1960s British top-boost amps: jangle and edge-of-breakup
description: A modelled British 30-watt guitar combo of the early 1960s with its treble boost, without a cabinet: a first valve whose two halves are the normal and the brilliant channels, the brilliant channel's small capacitor that passes the top, the treble boost's stage and cathode follower driving a treble and bass network, and four small European output pentodes in push-pull with no master and no feedback, biased by their shared cathode resistor, with the cut between their grids and a valve rectifier that sags. Normal and brilliant volumes, treble, bass, and cut, which jack is played or both joined, the treble boost in or out, a valve or a stiff supply, and a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuit is solved. It wants a cabinet after it, the speaker cabinet device. Modelled on the chiming class-A combo of the British beat groups, with its treble boost.

label: Swiss Roll Tape
summary: tape machine in the style of the 1970s Swiss studio recorders: saturation and glue, with wow and hiss
description: A modelled reel-to-reel tape machine: the signal is recorded onto tape and played back. The tape saturates softly, the highs first, with a third harmonic that the bias trades against the top end; the playback head adds its bump in the lows, which moves with the tape speed; and the transport adds wow, flutter, and hiss as far as their knobs are turned. Drive, tape speed (7.5, 15, 30 inches a second), four formulations of tape, bias, head bump, wow, flutter, hiss, output, and mix. The tape is a Jiles-Atherton model of magnetic hysteresis under a bias that dies away. Modelled on the Swiss multitrack studio recorder of the late 1970s, the machine most records of the following decade were tracked on.

label: Mid-Century Preamp
summary: valve mic preamp in the style of the mid-century studio preamps: warmth and drive for any track
description: A modelled valve saturator for any track: two triode stages and an output transformer. The second stage adds a second harmonic that grows with the level and flattens one side of the wave when it is driven hard; the first joins in when the gain switch is up; the transformer's core fills on low notes and thickens them. Gain switch, drive, bias, which moves the balance of even and odd harmonics, a tone before the valves and one after, mix, and output, with switches for the valves, the transformer, and an automatic gain that keeps a tone at -12 dBFS as loud as it went in wherever the drive stands, and a quality switch for how far above the sample rate the circuits are solved. In stereo, each channel through its own circuits. Modelled on the valve line amplifier in each channel of an American recording console of the 1960s, with the output transformer of a valve microphone preamplifier.

label: Parallel Passive EQ
summary: parallel passive valve EQ in the style of the late-1990s American mastering units: wide, sweet bells and shelves for mixes and masters
description: A modelled stereo valve equaliser whose four bands stand side by side rather than one after another: each a coil and a capacitor, a bell or a shelf, switched to cut, out or boost, with a gain that is flat at its bottom and a bandwidth that also sets how far the band reaches, and in shelf mode a dip or a bump beside the shelf. Bands at one frequency do not add up. Passive high and low pass filters, a trim, and two valve amplifiers and an output transformer that give back what the network loses. At two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Class-A Tube Strip
summary: class-A valve channel strip in the style of the late-1990s American boutique units: clean valve gain, smooth optical compression and a wide four-band EQ for vocals and bass
description: A modelled class-A valve channel strip of the late 1990s: a line or microphone input and a high-pass, a valve preamplifier in a loop of heavy feedback with a High Gain switch, an optical compressor whose lamp lights a photoresistor against a ratio pot, its attack and release on two pots and a faster attack switch, and a four-band discrete equaliser (a bass and a treble shelf, two sweeping mids with x10 and Q switches) that can go ahead of the compressor or into its sidechain; then the output. At two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Tube Console Strip
summary: valve channel strip in the style of the modern American tube strips: warm preamp, three-band EQ and one-knob opto for vocals and instruments
description: A modelled modern American valve channel strip: a valve microphone preamplifier of two triode stages with a gain switch and a level knob that warms and then drives it, an 80 Hz low cut, a three-band equaliser of a low shelf, a swept mid bell and a high shelf, an optical compressor with one knob that also sets its make-up gain, and the output. The preamplifier at two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Tube Vocal Strip
summary: valve vocal channel in the style of the late-1990s American vocal boxes: opto before the valves, passive peak-and-dip EQ, de-esser and limiter
description: A modelled American valve vocal channel of the late 1990s: a line input transformer, a 6 dB low cut and the input pot, a passive optical compressor ahead of the valves with stepped attack and release, a two-triode preamplifier whose gain switch sets its feedback, a passive equaliser of a low peak, a mid dip and a high peak on stepped coils, a passive optical de-esser or limiter, a valve line amplifier and the output transformer. The preamplifier at two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Yankee Desk Strip
summary: discrete console channel in the style of the American desks: proportional-Q stepped EQ, VCA compressor, op-amp drive
description: A modelled channel of the American discrete consoles: a high-pass and a low-pass on pots that can go into the compressor's sidechain, a four-band equaliser of stepped switches whose bands narrow as they rise (the outer bands a shelf, a bell or a cut, a range that halves or quarters every step), a VCA compressor with feedback or feed-forward detection, a hard or soft knee and a parallel share, and the discrete op-amp output stage driven into its rails, its character setting how readily the highs clip. At two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Albion Desk Strip
summary: transistor console channel in the style of the late-1960s British class-A desks: inductor EQ, diode-bridge compressor and limiter, transformer drive
description: A modelled channel of the British class-A consoles of the late 1960s and early 1970s: a low and a high cut, an inductor equaliser (a low shelf, a mid bell with a ten-way Q and a high shelf, each with an off position) ahead of the compressor or after the limiter, a diode-bridge compressor and limiter on stepped switches with a dry share, and a transformer-coupled class-A drive stage with a character network ahead of it. At two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Tube Grand Channel
summary: valve channel in the style of the 1990s American leveling and program EQ racks: smooth one-knob leveling, a saturation knob and a four-band passive EQ
description: A modelled American valve channel of the 1990s: a levelling compressor whose one knob sets how much and how hard, with three attacks and releases and a saturation knob for its valve's headroom, and a passive equaliser of four bands, each boost or cut on seven stepped coils with its width, and low and high cuts, with its valve make-up; the order switchable, a parallel mix. At four times the sample rate.

label: Tube Leveling Amp
summary: valve leveling amplifier in the style of the 1990s American racks: smooth one-knob leveling whose release follows the program, a saturation knob, for vocals, bass and buses
description: A modelled American valve leveling amplifier of the 1990s: one knob sets how much and how hard, its ratio growing with the reduction; three attacks and releases, the slower ones following the program; a valve after the cell whose headroom the saturation knob moves, a low cut on the input or the detector, a parallel mix. At four times the sample rate.

label: Tube Program EQ
summary: passive valve program EQ in the style of the 1990s American racks: four broad stepped bands that boost or cut, shelves and bells, for tracks and mixes
description: A modelled American passive program equaliser of the 1990s with its valve make-up: four bands, each boost or cut on seven stepped coils with its width, the outer two shelf or bell, and low and high cuts. At four times the sample rate.

label: Danish Program EQ
summary: passive valve program EQ in the style of the Danish studio units: a low shelf that boosts and cuts at once and a broad or sharp high peak, for tracks and mixes
description: A modelled Danish passive program equaliser of the late 1980s and 1990s with its valve make-up: a low shelf at four places that boosts and cuts at once, a high peak at ten places from 1 to 16 kHz whose width is a knob, and a high cut at three. At four times the sample rate.

label: Danish Midrange EQ
summary: passive valve mid-range EQ in the style of the Danish studio units: broad stepped low and high peaks and a dip, for shaping a voice or an instrument's middle
description: A modelled Danish passive mid-range equaliser of the late 1980s and 1990s with its valve make-up: a low peak at five places, a dip at eleven and a high peak at five, on stepped coils. At four times the sample rate.

label: Danish Multiband Compressor
summary: three-band opto compressor in the style of the Danish studio units: gentle crossovers that sum flat, smooth band leveling for mixes and masters
description: A modelled Danish stereo three-band optical compressor of the 1990s: two crossovers of one resistor and capacitor each, so the bands sum back flat, and in each band an optical cell in a passive divider lit by a sidechain common to both channels, with its threshold, ratio, attack, release and gain; the output, a balance, a parallel mix, mid/side.

label: Danish Tube Channel
summary: valve channel in the style of the Danish studio units: passive program and mid EQs and a smooth opto compressor, either order
description: A modelled Danish valve channel of the late 1980s and 1990s: a passive program equaliser with a low shelf that boosts and cuts at once and a broadening high peak, a passive mid-range equaliser of a low peak, a dip and a high peak on stepped coils, and an optical compressor with fixed and manual timing, each section with its valve make-up; the order switchable, a parallel mix, mid/side. The equalisers at four times the sample rate.

label: British Rock EQ
summary: transistor console channel in the style of the late-1960s British rock desks: resonant bass, bold mids and gritty drive for drums, guitars and vocals
description: A modelled British console channel of the late 1960s: a transistor preamplifier with stepped gain that grits up as it is turned up, then a passive equaliser of coils and capacitors: a bass that peaks on a large coil at four frequencies or cuts the lows in five steps, a mid that peaks or dips at eight frequencies, and a stepped treble shelf, all in one divider so that they lean on one another; then the make-up stage, which clips on one side first, the output transformer, and the level. At two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Germanium Mastering EQ
summary: stereo mastering equaliser in the style of the late-1960s British console EQs on germanium amplifiers: stepped bells and shelves, gentle filters, transformer weight
description: A modelled stereo mastering equaliser of germanium-transistor amplifiers in the style of the British studio console equalisers of the late 1960s: four bands of stepped frequency (a bass and a treble that peak or shelve, two presence bells), each on an amplifier of its own with a stepped gain and a range switch, its width following its gain; a stepped high and low pass; and the transformers, the input's core giving low notes a faint third harmonic. At four times the sample rate.

label: 1960s Studio EQ
summary: seven-band stepped graphic EQ in the style of a 1960s American label's in-house studio EQs: broad interacting inductor bands, a hard-clipping make-up amp
description: A modelled seven-band stepped graphic equaliser in the style of the in-house equalisers of a 1960s American record label's studios: passive coils and capacitors in two interleaved constant-resistance networks (50 Hz to 12.5 kHz, -8 to +8 dB in whole steps), so a band's width follows its gain and two bands of a network pull on each other; a make-up amplifier that clips hard at its rails, and the transformers, the input's core giving low notes a third harmonic. At four times the sample rate.

label: 1960s Mastering EQ
summary: stereo disc-mastering EQ in the style of a 1960s American label's in-house unit: broad stepped coil bands at full or half speed, mid/side, steep disc-cutting filters
description: A modelled two-channel seven-band stepped mastering equaliser in the style of the disc-mastering equaliser of a 1960s American record label: the studio unit's passive interleaved coil networks, each band dipping or peaking 1 to 8 dB at its frequency or an octave lower at half speed; left and right or mid and side; steep elliptic disc-cutting filters at 70 Hz and 15 kHz; the make-up amplifier's hard rails and the transformers. At four times the sample rate.

label: Three-Prong EQ
summary: console channel equaliser in the style of the early-1970s British desks: broad musical shelves, coil mids that lean on each other, stacking filters, rail saturation
description: A modelled British console channel equaliser of the early 1970s: four bands on faders at four stepped frequencies each, a broad low and high shelf on one amplifier and two coil-and-capacitor mids on another, so that each pair leans on one another and a mid's Q follows its gain; three high-pass and three low-pass buttons that can be pressed together; and the output amplifier, which the saturation knob drives into its rails. At two or four times the sample rate, as late at both.

label: Five-Circuit Saturator
summary: five-circuit saturator in the style of the classic studio colour boxes: valve, transformer, class-A and pentode drive for anything
description: A modelled saturator of five circuits, each a gain stage of a piece of studio hardware worked out from its parts: a tape recorder's valve preamplifier, warm and even; a British console's transistor microphone amplifier, bright and gritty; a class-A console channel, thick and rounded; and a valve distortion unit's pentode, edgy and buzzing, and the same valve run as a triode, fat and smooth. Drive, a low cut and a tone tilt before the stage, a high cut after it, gentle or steep, a punish switch that drives it 20 dB harder, a thump at the low cut, mix, and output with an automatic gain that holds the level as the drive goes up. In stereo, each channel through its own circuit, the stage at two, four, eight or sixteen times the sample rate, as late at each.

label: 1950s Tube Mixer
summary: valve microphone mixer in the style of the 1950s American broadcast amplifiers: warm, thick drive with simple bass and treble
description: A modelled valve microphone mixer of the 1950s American broadcast and studio amplifiers, as a saturator: a line input, or a microphone input through its transformer, the channel's gain into a high-mu preamplifier valve, the mixer's simple bass and treble, the master level into a single-ended output valve on its output transformer, which rounds and then flattens the top of the wave, a mix, and the unit's own hiss. In stereo, each channel through its own valves, at four times the sample rate.

label: Quickdraw FET
summary: FET limiting amp in the style of the late-1960s American studio limiters: fast, aggressive peaks for drums and vocals
description: A modelled peak limiter built on a field-effect transistor: the transistor is the lower leg of a divider at the input and turns the audio down as the sidechain, which listens after it, lifts its gate. It has no threshold knob: the input knob drives the audio into a fixed threshold and the output knob makes up the level. Attack and release, both fastest at the top of their travel, with an attack from a few milliseconds down to a tenth of one, and a button for each ratio, 4, 8, 12, or 20 to 1, none of them, or all four at once, which pumps and distorts. It can listen to another track by sidechain. Modelled on the black-faced American transistor limiting amplifier of the late 1960s, the usual fast, aggressive compressor for drums, vocals, and bass.

label: Low Orbit Echo
summary: tape echo with spring reverb in the style of the 1970s Japanese tape echoes: dub and swirling repeats
description: A modelled tape echo: a loop of tape that never stops, one record head, and three playback heads at fixed distances along it, with a spring reverb beside it. A twelve-position selector chooses which heads play and whether the springs do. The repeat rate is the motor's speed, so turning it bends the pitch of every echo still on the tape, and it can be set from the project's tempo instead. Intensity feeds the heads back to the record head: each pass is recorded again, so repeats darken and compress, and past about 70 with one head they grow until the tape saturates and the machine sings by itself; more heads sing sooner, all three by about 53. Bass and treble on the echoes, echo and reverb volume, input level, wow, flutter, hiss, and the dry signal passed beside it with no delay. The tape is the tape machine's model of hysteresis. Modelled on the Japanese tape echo of the middle 1970s with three heads and a spring tank, the echo of dub and of space rock.

label: Duress Compressor
summary: character compressor in the style of the 1990s American digital-analogue units: dist modes, Nuke, vocals and drums
description: A modelled character compressor for vocals, drums, bass and rooms: an input knob that drives a fixed threshold and an output after it, attacks from under a tenth of a millisecond to some 40 ms and releases from a twentieth of a second to several, ratios of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 10 and 20 to 1, each with its own knee, and Nuke, a brickwall; a detector that can hear less of the low end or more of the sibilant band, and a stereo link; a high-pass in the audio; and two harmonic generators, Dist 2, a second harmonic that grows with the reduction, and Dist 3, a clipping stage driven harder for a third. A mix for parallel compression. Modelled on the American digitally controlled analogue compressors of the middle 1990s.

label: Punch Bus Compressor
summary: RMS bus compressor in the style of the 2000s American discrete units: punchy glue for the mix and drum buses
description: A modelled stereo bus compressor of discrete op-amps, VCAs and an output transformer, for a mix bus or a drum bus: an RMS detector in each channel, ratios of 1.5 to infinity to 1, attacks of 0.03 to 30 ms, releases of 0.05 to 2 s on a switch or a variable one, three knees, a weighting in the detector that hears the low end less and the top more for a punchier sound, feed-forward or feedback, and a link between the two channels by a share from independent to 100 % through a filter. Modelled on the American bus compressors of the late 1990s and 2000s.

label: Desk Glue Bus Compressor
summary: VCA bus compressor in the style of the 1980s British large-format consoles: glue for the mix and drum buses
description: A modelled bus compressor built on a voltage-controlled amplifier, for gluing a mix bus or a drum bus: a threshold, ratios of 2, 4, and 10 to 1, an attack of 0.1 to 30 ms and a release of 0.1 to 1.2 s on switches, with an automatic release that lets a short peak go quickly and a long passage slowly, and a make-up gain. One peak detector serves both channels, so the stereo image holds still. Its timing is the circuit's network of a diode, resistances, and capacitors, solved exactly. With a high-pass in the sidechain, a mix of the compressed with what went in, a switch for where the detector listens, ahead of the gain element or behind it, and a sidechain from another track. Modelled on the stereo compressor in the centre section of a large British mixing console of the 1980s.

label: 1976 VCA Compressor
summary: VCA compressor in the style of the 1970s American units: fast, punchy, a soft knee, for drums and bass
description: A modelled compressor built on a true-RMS detector and a voltage-controlled amplifier, for hitting a snare, a kick or a bass hard: a threshold, a compression knob from 1 to 1 up to infinity to 1, and an output gain. It has no attack or release: the detector averages the square of the signal, so it takes hold the faster the further over the threshold a sound is and lets go at a steady rate in dB, and it puts a thump on a drum. With a high-pass on what the detector hears and a mix of the compressed with what went in. Modelled on the American feed-forward compressor of the middle 1970s, the one with the infinity on its dial.

label: Pitch Correction
summary: pitch correction: tunes a voice to the scale, natural or hard
description: Corrects a voice's pitch as it plays: the pitch is heard every 5 ms and moved to the nearest note of the project's scale guide, or of a scale chosen here. The retune speed is how fast it gets there: at 0 the voice jumps from note to note and its vibrato is gone, the effect known from records; at 50 to 100 ms it sounds sung in tune, its scoops and vibrato kept. Humanize retunes a held note more slowly, amount corrects part of the way, transpose and formant move the voice and its vowels' colour, and detune aims at another tuning than A 440. The voice is made again a period at a time (TD-PSOLA), which keeps its tone; where no pitch is heard it passes as it came. For one voice at a time: a vocal, a lead, a bass line. It plays 30 to 60 ms late, by its range, which the mix makes up for.

label: Echo Lad
summary: multi-style echo in the style of the 2000s studio echo boxes: tape, oil can and early digital delays in one
description: A modelled multi-style echo, for vocals, guitars, keys, synths and drums: one echo with a choice of four machines to play through. Studio tape, a two-track machine used for slap and echo, soft and steady; tape echo, the single-head 1960s tape echo with its preamp, dark and wavering; oil can, the 1960s drum-in-oil echo, narrow, uneven and wavering; early digital, the 1980s rack delay, clean to its converters' rails. Single, Dual, Ping-pong and Rhythm feels, Groove and Feel to swing and push the repeats, saturation into the machine, low and high cuts in the loop, and a time that glides as a tape transport does, synced to the tempo or free.

label: Formant Shifter
summary: vocal pitch and formant shifter in the style of the vocal transformers of 2010s pop: a bigger or smaller voice, a robot on one note
description: A modelled vocal pitch and formant shifter in the style of the vocal transformers of 2010s pop and hip-hop, for vocals, raps and spoken lines: the pitch moved up to an octave either way and the formants, the voice's size, moved apart from it, a period at a time (TD-PSOLA), so a voice keeps its tone. Transpose moves it, Quantize first draws it to the nearest semitone, Robot holds it on one note; Link moves the formants with the pitch; a valve-like Drive and a Mix. For one voice at a time. It plays 50 ms late, which the mix makes up for.

label: Micro Pitch Doubler
summary: pitch-shift doubler in the style of the 1980s studio rack harmonisers: wide, still doubling for vocals, guitars, and synths
description: A modelled studio micro-shift doubler, for lead and backing vocals, guitars, synths, and whole mixes: two pitch shifters a few cents up and a few cents down, each with a short delay of its own, one on each side, so that a sound is heard twice, a little apart in pitch and time, wide and still, without the wobble of a chorus. Three styles: I and II after the late-1980s American rack harmoniser's two micro-shift programs, I the grainier, III after the British rack pitch changer of the late 1970s, with longer delays and a harder splice. Detune and Delay scale the style's own shift and delays; Focus keeps the lows below it in the middle, unshifted.

label: Fourth Dimension Chorus
summary: BBD dimension chorus in the style of the late-1970s Japanese studio rack unit: wide, still stereo for pads, guitars, vocals, and mixes
description: A modelled studio dimension chorus, for pads, keys, clean guitars, vocals, and whole mixes: two bucket-brigade lines that one slow triangle sweeps in opposite directions, each mixed mostly into the other side and a little, turned over, into its own, beside the dry signal, so a sound widens and thickens without the wobble of a chorus. Four buttons, pressed alone or together as the unit allows: 1 and 2 sweep slowly, 2 the deeper, 3 and 4 faster and shallower, and 4 also mixes each line into its own side nearly as much as into the other, for the widest image; summed to mono, the lines then cancel. Modelled on the late-1970s Japanese studio rack unit.

label: June Chorus
summary: BBD chorus in the style of the early-1980s Japanese polysynths' chorus: lush stereo for synths, pads, and clean guitars
description: A modelled bucket-brigade chorus, for synths, pads, and clean guitars: two delay lines of 256 stages, each a chain of capacitors that a clock passes the signal along, so that the delay is the clock's rate. One triangle sweeps the two clocks in opposite directions, one line's delay growing as the other's shrinks, and the dry signal is mixed beside them, which spreads a mono sound wide. Two buttons, as the unit has: I sweeps slowly, II faster, and I and II together is a quick, shallow vibrato in both lines at once. The lines sample what comes in at their clock, so their images are heard on high notes, and their transfer adds a second harmonic and a little third. Rate and depth against the mode's own, a mix, a width, a stereo or summed input, drive, the lines' noise, and an output. Modelled on the chorus built into the Japanese six-voice polysynths of the early 1980s.

label: Lift Pedal
summary: one-transistor clean boost: more level, or an amp pushed into breakup
description: A modelled one-transistor clean boost, for guitar into an amplifier: a silicon transistor in common emitter with an unbypassed emitter resistor and a volume pot after it, the circuit most clean boosts are built on. It lifts a guitar by up to some 26 dB, cleanly at a guitar's level; a hot input flattens it, one side before the other, which pushes an amplifier's input into breaking up. One knob, the boost, and an output. Modelled on the small linear booster of the late 1960s.

label: Saucer Fuzz
summary: two-transistor fuzz in the style of the late-1960s British round fuzzes, germanium or silicon: thick fuzz that cleans up
description: A two-transistor fuzz for guitar, germanium or silicon: two transistors in common emitter fed back on each other, clipping hard and lopsided into a thick, buzzing sustain that cleans up as the guitar is turned down. Germanium is rounder and darker with a thinner bass at full fuzz; silicon has more gain and a brighter, more even edge. Fuzz, volume, the transistors, and an output; light or full quality. Modelled on the round fuzz pedal of the late 1960s and fitted to a model of it.

label: Mitten Fuzz
summary: four-stage sustaining fuzz in the style of the 1970s American big fuzz boxes: smooth wall of fuzz, long sustain, scooped tone
description: A four-stage sustaining fuzz for guitar and bass: a booster into two transistor stages that each clip softly and evenly, a tone stack that blends a low-pass and a high-pass with a scooped middle between them, and a recovery stage. A thick, smooth wall of fuzz with a long, singing sustain. Sustain, tone, volume, and an output; light or full quality. Modelled on the big American fuzz of the early 1970s.

label: Burrow Distortion
summary: op-amp distortion into diodes in the style of the late-1970s American hard-clipping pedals, with a filter knob: grit to thick distortion
description: An op-amp distortion for guitar: a slow op-amp whose gain the distortion knob raises, its bandwidth narrowing as it does, clipping into two diodes to ground, then a filter knob that darkens it. From a gritty overdrive to a thick, saturated distortion. Distortion, filter, volume, and an output; light or full quality. Modelled on the American op-amp distortion pedal of the late 1970s.

label: Teardrop Wah
summary: inductor wah in the style of the late-1960s American wah pedals: a pedal to sweep or automate, or an auto-wah by envelope or LFO
description: An inductor wah pedal for guitar, keys and bass: a resonant peak that the pedal sweeps from some 480 Hz at the heel to 2 kHz at the toe, the lows held under it. The pedal is a parameter to automate or to map a MIDI expression pedal to; or an envelope follower or an oscillator moves it, as an auto-wah. Pedal, mode, depth, rate, sensitivity, and an output. Modelled on the American wah of the late 1960s.

label: Squash Compressor
summary: OTA compressor pedal in the style of the 1970s American squash boxes: even picking, long sustain, squashed clean attacks
description: A compressor pedal for guitar: a transconductance gain cell whose gain a detector of its own output pulls down, fast to clamp and slow to let go. It evens out picking, lifts a fading note into a long sustain, and squashes the attack of a clean funk or country part. Sustain, volume, and an output. Modelled on the orange and red compressor pedals of the 1970s.

label: Whiny Shifter
summary: pitch-shift pedal in the style of the 1990s expression-pedal shifters: octaves, dive bombs and drop tunings
description: A pitch-shift pedal for guitar: an expression pedal sweeps the shift between a heel and a toe interval, up to two octaves either way, for octave leads, dive bombs, harmonies and detuned doubling, and drops a tuning without retuning. Polyphonic and 10 ms late whatever the interval, or 16 ms to join low chords; a classic character glitches as the early digital pedals did. Pedal, heel, toe, mix, character, glide, an octave-down and a semitone-up layer, an output, and the latency.

label: Chug Rig
summary: modern metal rig: gate, chug, low dirt, tight amp, and cab in one
description: A modern metal guitar rig in one device, from a DI to a miked cabinet, each section switched by itself: a gate; chug, which cuts the lows for a moment after each pick so palm mutes stay tight; low dirt, a hard-clipped fuzz of the lows added under the guitar; a high-gain amp that evens out the level it is given, clips hard after a band-pass round 1.4 kHz, with drive, low, mid, high, and presence; a lo-fi band-pass; its own cabinet; low and high cuts; and mono or stereo. It holds the audio back by 32 frames.

label: Guitar Auto-EQ
summary: guitar auto-EQ: learns your guitar and turns it toward a pickup's DI or a saved tone profile
description: An equaliser that turns the guitar it is given toward a target guitar. Listen learns the guitar's tone from five seconds of playing; the equaliser is the difference between that and the target, a passive pickup's DI of our own or a tone profile, a guitar learned and saved. Amount sets how far it goes (100 % an even match), smooth how smooth the equaliser is, from a twelfth of an octave to more than half of one, and an output. It does nothing until it has learned a guitar, and holds nothing back.

label: Berserk Amp
summary: three-channel valve head with a temper switch: thick, dark modern high gain
description: A modelled three-channel high-gain valve head with a temper switch, and a cabinet that can be switched off: an input valve, the temper's voicing and the gain pot, a second valve, a third on the high and insane channels, a clipping stage that clips one side of the wave first, a fourth stage into a cathode follower, a bass, middle, and treble stack after the clipping, the master, and the power stage's loop with its depth and presence. Clean, high, and insane channels; calm, fierce, and rage tempers, each a set of the circuit's values fitted to a reference. It holds the audio back by 38 frames.

label: Leviathan Rig
summary: heavy rig: a gate, two drive pedals, three valve amps, a nine-band EQ, and cab in one
description: A heavy guitar rig in one device, each section switched by itself: a gate, a downward expander; an overdrive and a distortion pedal; one of three amps, clean, rust and hot, valve circuits of ours revoiced toward a digital amp suite's, with gain, low, mid, high, master, presence, depth (the lows round the speaker's resonance), bright, and level; a nine-band EQ, a low shelf, seven bells an octave apart and a high shelf; and a cabinet for each amp. It holds the audio back by 76 frames.

label: Djent Amp
summary: tight heavy rig: a gate, a drive pedal, three valve amps, a nine-band EQ, and cab in one
description: A tight, heavy guitar rig in one device, each section switched by itself: a gate, a downward expander; a drive pedal with drive, bright, volume, and a six-place attack switch that leaves the lows out of the clipping; one of three amps, clean, rhythm and lead, valve circuits of ours revoiced toward a digital amp suite's, with gain, low, mid, high, presence, master, a voice switch each, a boost on the clean, and level; a nine-band EQ with a high-pass and a low-pass; and a cabinet for each amp. It holds the audio back by 76 frames.

label: Untitled Amp
summary: tight heavy rig: two gates, a drive, a boost, a two-gain valve amp, a nine-band EQ, and cab in one
description: A tight, heavy guitar rig in one device, each section switched by itself: a gate, a downward expander; a gate pedal; a drive pedal with drive, tone and level; a boost that keeps the lows out of the amp; one amp, a valve circuit of ours revoiced toward a digital amp suite's, with a low or high input, pull, gain I and gain II, low, mid, high, presence, master and level; a nine-band EQ with a high-pass and a low-pass; and its cabinet. It holds the audio back by 76 frames.

label: A2 Modeller Amp
summary: a Neural Amp Modeler capture of an amp, a pedal or a rig, played from its .nam file
description: A tone captured with Neural Amp Modeler, an amp, a pedal or a whole rig, played from its .nam file (NAM's A2, Lite and Full, and A1's WaveNets and LSTMs), which is kept with the project; with an input gain, a calibration to the level the tone was captured at, the output levelled by its loudness, and an output gain. It holds the audio back by 64 frames, and 128 where the model's rate is not the project's.

label: Hush Gate
summary: noise gate pedal: silence between high-gain riffs
description: A noise gate pedal for high-gain guitar: it shuts the hiss and hum of a driven amplifier between notes and lets each note through whole. It listens through a band of 80 Hz to 4 kHz, so neither hum nor hiss holds it open, or to another track by sidechain, such as a dry guitar before the amplifier. It opens at the threshold over the attack, smoothly, stays open for the hold once the note falls the hysteresis under the threshold, and closes over the release evenly in decibels, the way a string dies away, to the range. Put it after the drive and before the delay.

label: Comet Flanger
summary: bucket-brigade flanger in the style of the 1970s analogue flanger pedals: a sweeping jet-plane comb
description: A modelled bucket-brigade flanger, for guitars, keys, drums, and whole mixes: one short chain of capacitors that a clock passes the signal along, between a compressor and an expander, mixed with the dry signal, which cuts a comb of notches that sweeps as the clock does. Manual sets the delay, from a fraction of a millisecond to some ten; width how far a slow oscillator sweeps it from there; speed how fast, from a sweep over a minute long to five a second; regeneration feeds the wet path back for a ringing, metallic jet; mix sets the two paths, deepest at the middle. Modelled on the rack and pedal flangers of the late 1970s and early 1980s.

label: Karlavagnen Analyzer
summary: analyzer: loudness, true peak, spectrum and stereo, as a master is measured
description: Measures what passes through it and changes nothing: loudness as the streaming services read it (momentary, short-term, integrated, and its range), true peak, correlation, the spectrum and the stereo image. The master has one of its own, opened from the Loudness readout in the top bar; this one measures a track, or a place in a chain. Agents read the same numbers with the loudness command.

label: Solvind EQ
summary: listening EQ: what hides is tamed, what is hidden brought up
description: An equaliser that listens, the mastering family's: many times a second it works out which bands of what passes hide the bands about them, on a model of hearing, and turns those down and the hidden ones up, so a master or a bus is clearer and more even without a fixed curve. Recover and Tame set how far each way, Bias how the spectrum is split between them, Brighten whether the unmasking leans to the highs or the lows, Boost the balance of a louder or quieter playback, and two limits where it acts; the loudness is held, so it is not heard louder. 21 ms late, which the renderer takes out.

label: Trollspegeln Imager
summary: stereo imager: width by band, the lows in mono
description: A stereo imager for the master and for buses, the mastering family's: how wide each of four bands is, from mono through as it came to its side doubled, split where the crossover splits so at every width 1 it changes nothing; and the lows folded to mono below a frequency, as a master's should be.

label: Plejaderna Multiband
summary: multiband compressor: four bands, each held or lifted on its own
description: A multiband compressor for the master and for buses, the mastering family's: four bands, split where the crossover splits and summing back flat, each a compressor over its threshold, by its ratio, or under 1:1 one that lifts it, with its own attack, release, gain, solo and mute. A new one changes nothing until a band is set to.

label: Pulsar Shaper
summary: volume shaper: a drawn duck in time with the song, as a sidechain pumps
description: A volume curve drawn over a stretch of the song, from a sixteenth to two bars, that turns a track down and up again in time: the pumping of a sidechained compressor under a kick, with no sidechain, or gates and swells. A second curve can move a filter's cutoff in the same time. Each cycle starts on the song's grid or with each note; ready shapes start it, and its curves are drawn.

label: Glimmer Chorus
summary: ensemble chorus: up to eight voices, swept, with feedback
description: An ensemble chorus: one to four pairs of voices between two delay times, swept by a slow sine and spread across the stereo field, with feedback through a band of the wet sound, from a gentle widening to a ringing, flanging shimmer. Its rate can follow the song's tempo.

label: Tidvatten Compressor
summary: upward and downward compressor: three bands, the loud pushed down, the quiet lifted
description: A three-band upward and downward compressor, for sound design and for loud, dense sounds: each band is pushed down above its push line and lifted below its lift line at once, so what is loud comes down and what is quiet comes up, with Depth for how much of it is heard and Time for how fast it moves. Vital's multiband compressor imports as it.

label: Himlavalv Limiter
summary: true-peak limiter: loud and clean, for the master and buses
description: A limiter for the master and for buses, made to be heard as little as it can: nothing passes its ceiling, between the samples as on them, as the streaming services read a peak. It looks ahead so the gain is down when a peak arrives, and turns down in two parts: a slow one that holds the level that keeps coming back, so a steady tone is not bent and loud music does not pump, and a fast one that takes what is left of each peak and lets go at once, so a lone snare does not duck what follows. Its character goes from Clear to Push; its lookahead is how late it makes the audio.

label: Tuner
summary: chromatic tuner: the note and cents of a held string
description: A chromatic tuner for guitar, bass, and anything that holds a note: it shows the note it hears and how many cents sharp or flat, against a reference for A4, and passes the audio as it came or mutes it while tuning, as a tuner pedal does. It reads a steady string to within half a cent from a dropped low D up. Agents read it with the tuner command.

label: Quack Filter
summary: envelope filter in the style of the 1970s auto-wahs, through a ladder that each note opens: funk quack
description: A modelled envelope filter, the auto-wah, for funk guitar, clav, bass, and synths: the four-pole transistor ladder of the classic monosynth, whose corner an envelope follower moves up by how loud the input is, so that each note opens the filter as it starts and lets it close as it dies away. Cutoff, resonance, and drive are the ladder's; amount sets how far a note opens it; the mode is slow, a swell that lingers, or fast, a snap that falls back; and a mix against the dry signal.
